crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Aug 23: AP reported no confirmed attacks in the Strait of Hormuz over the prior 48 hours, but shipping traffic remained reduced. AP reported Iran's security chief said support for new US economic measures would be treated as an act of war; Iran and Oman are discussing management of the strait, likely including transit fees, while Pakistan's army chief is due in Tehran to revive talks. The 60-day US-Iran deadline passed without a settlement. Brent was $93.47 (Yahoo Finance, Aug 23) and TTF was $66.00 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, Aug 21; +3.7%). Crisis level remains 4 (High); base is 5%, stress 55%, tail 40%.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: AP reported no confirmed attacks in Hormuz over 48 hours and Iran-Oman management talks continue, but the 60-day US-Iran deadline passed without a settlement. Brent moves toward $75-85 only if a workable reopening follows; Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: No workable full-reopening agreement emerges: AP reported traffic remains reduced and an Iranian authority listed vessels facing future restrictions. Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Iran's security chief called support for new US economic measures an act of war; AP reported transit restrictions despite no confirmed attacks in 48 hours. A breakdown in Iran-Oman talks could renew full closure and spill into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $93.47 (Aug 23, Yahoo Finance BZ=F; +2.69%) as AP reported reduced Hormuz traffic, no confirmed attacks in 48 hours, and an Iranian warning over sanctions support. Working range $75-85 base (signed workable deal); $78-95 stress (conditional routing); $105-135+ tail (renewed closure).
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters September-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $21.22/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Aug 14), also carried on Aug 23. Qatar force majeure is carried through mid-September from the Reuters Jul 23 notice; the reported mid-October extension remains unconfirmed.
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> 63.58/MWh (Jul 24, MacroMicro) -> 66.00 EUR/MWh (Aug 21, Yahoo Finance TTF=F; +3.7%) as reduced Hormuz traffic, Iranian transit restrictions and the unresolved Iran-Oman arrangement kept European gas flows at risk. The marker remains elevated versus the pre-crisis baseline while Qatar LNG force majeure persists.
priceNarratives.Credit: iTraxx Asia IG est. ~138bp (Aug 5, -2bp); ASEAN HY est. ~475bp (-8bp), both carried pending fresher EM credit data. The scenario split is base 5%, stress 55%, tail 40% after AP reported reduced traffic, Iranian transit restrictions and no signed reopening; no confirmed attack was reported in the prior 48 hours.
